utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody, and thank you for coming to this Status Conference. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-74-A, The Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Before we begin, I want to make sure that the appellants can follow the proceedings in a language that they understand. I start with you, Mr. Prlic, as usual.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Yes, I'm able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prlic. Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can follow the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Coric, sorry. Mr. Coric, yeah. Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I'm able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I now have the appearances for the parties, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Barbara Goy, Case Manager Janet Stewart, and legal intern, Ashrutha Rai.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I thank you. Before calling appearances for the Defence, I need to give some information. First I note that on the 20th of December --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Excuse me, Mr. President. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Sorry to interrupt to you, but I'm hearing you in B/C/S. My B/C/S is rusty so if I could hear you in English, it would be more wonderful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I have, as you see, made a big headway in speaking in B/C/S, but I can't fix it myself. I need technical assistance.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There must be a headset turned on to B/C/S somewhere near the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have some assistance. Because here I have four headsets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Karnavas, I am informed that this is simply technical. And, of course, he is receiving me in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] So you're having a technical problem on your end or my end?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes, as long as necessary. This has to be fixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I can say it myself. One or more of the B/C/S interpreters, could you speak, please speak out so that we test exactly what is happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, Mr. Karnavas, I'll speak in English now again. Are you receiving me in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, so we can proceed. I take this opportunity to thank the B/C/S booth for having come forward to assist and also the technical people who have solved the problem. So let me go back to where I was before. I have called for the representations for the Prosecution. It's my turn now to turn to call appearances for the Defence. But before I do that, I need to point out that on the 20th of December, 2016, counsel for Mr. Pusic requested to attend this Status Conference by videolink from Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Mr. Pusic has provided his consent for the Status Conference to be held in his absence and not has not provided any objections to his counsel's participation in this way. For the record, I can see his counsel on the videolink. On the 11th of January, 2017, counsel for Mr. Prlic also requested to participate in today's Status Conference via conference from Phnom Penh in Cambodia. Mr. Prlic has indicated that he has no objection to this. And under Rule 65 bis (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I am hereby granting both requests. Moreover, I note that on the 12th of January, 2017 counsel for Mr. Praljak, who is present here today, indicated that they are not in a position to attend today's Status Conference, and on the next day, Mr. Praljak himself filed a waiver to that extent, accepting that the proceedings continue without the presence and intervention of his lawyers. That is also granted. I also take this opportunity to thank the Tribunal's staff as well as the staff of the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia for making a video-conference link from two different locations possible for this Status Conference. Now could I have the appearances for Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Michael Karnavas, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you assisted by anyone, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] No, I'm by myself. I'm a solo -- I'm flying solo today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Okay, thank you. Land safely. Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. For Mr. Stojic, represented by Senka Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Mr. Praljak, as we said, waived his right to be assisted by counsel today. Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. General Petkovic is represented by Vesna Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PLAVEC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Drazen Plavec appearing for Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And for Mr. Pusic. Please raise your voice because I can barely hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation][Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honour. Fahrudin Ibrisimovic appearing for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, this Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This rule requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the last Status Conference has been held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two purposes: First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions and for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical conditions of each one of them; and, secondly, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case as well as to inform the general public of what is going on. I note that the last Status Conference was held on 19th September 2016, and today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order signed by me and issued on the 17th of November, 2016. I'll come to one of the major purposes of this Status Conference. I'm going to inquire into the status of the detention conditions and health situation of the appellants. If any one of you, Mr. Prlic and each one of you, wish this discussion to take place in closed session, please let me know now. Would anyone like me to close the session and discuss the questions of your health and detention conditions in private or can I proceed? Are you all hearing me and understanding what I'm asking? All right, I see all the appellants nodding. So I take it that there is no need to go into closed session, and I will continue accordingly in an open session. Mr. Prlic, do you wish to raise any matters?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I have no complaint to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you very much, Mr. Prlic. Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no issues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And counsel for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation][Via videolink] Your Honour, we have no issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. I will now go into the next item which is informing everyone, including the public, about recent procedural history. All of the appellants' briefs in this case were filed on the 12th of January of two years ago, of 2015. The Defence and Prosecution's respondent's brief were filed on 7th May 2015 and the respective reply briefs were filed on the 29th of May, 2015. I note that the Appeals Chamber has issued an order on 15th December 2016 ordering that the appeal hearing will take place on 20 to 24 and then from 27 to 28 of March, 2017. There have been three other public filings by the Appeals Chamber since the previous Status Conference. The first goes back to the 26th of October, 2016, when the Appeals Chamber issued an order concerning non-receipt of funds addressing the non-receipt of funds due to the Tribunal from Mr. Praljak. Second was on the 1st of December, 2016 the Appeals Chamber lifted the confidentiality of the decision on Valentin Coric's request for provisional release, and the public redacted version of the decision was filed. And, finally, third, as I have already mentioned, the Scheduling Order for this Status Conference was filed on 17th of November of last year. I also note that there are no public motions pending before the Appeals Chamber at this time. Having said that, I come to the last part of the Status Conference, which -- where I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise. I start, as usual, with the Prosecution. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, just one very brief matter. We're grateful to the Chamber for issuing the Scheduling Order on the 15th of December giving all of the parties ample evidence of the dates of the upcoming hearing. It is very helpful for us. In that order, the Chamber has referred to coming orders regarding the modalities and the questions, and in respect of the modalities, that is, the scheduling of the hearings themselves, during the course of that week, we just wanted to respectfully direct the Chamber to the Scheduling Orders that have been used in the past and used in a couple of the other big -- numerous appellate cases, Popovic and also the MOS case, Sainovic and others. Those differ slightly in the respect of times allocated among the parties but in general provide what we think is a useful template or example that the Prosecution would suggest the Chamber consider in organising the hearings in this case. In addition, just again, and I know you're expecting this, the questions are going to be very key in all of this, particularly as Your Honour may know, it's a very busy time for us. On the 15th of March, just five days before this hearing starts, the Prosecution is filing its response brief in another very large appeal. And in this era of down sizing, virtually all of our staff are working on both cases. And so the greater amount of time in advance that we have to be sure to address the Chamber's questions, I think would be beneficial not only to the Prosecution but to the Chamber as well. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stringer. I can assure you your words haven't fallen on deaf ears. We are actively engaged in preparing all this and will come back to you and the appellants, of course, in the near future and as early as possible. I go through the Defence lawyers. Or the appellants themselves. I start with Mr. Prlic. Do you have anything to -- any issue that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: The same as Prosecutor, but I received the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, all right. And when I mention the accused, I'm also asking counsel, please. So if you wish to add anything, just make me a sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I confer with Dr. Prlic, Mr. President. And I appreciate Mr. Stringer raising the issue because we certainly would have raised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. I have no doubt and I appreciate. So Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence of Mr. Stojic was also concerned about having enough time to prepare, but since we have received answers to these questions, we have nothing further to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've had a long time to prepare. The only difference now is that you know when the hearing is going to take place, and very soon you will know how much time allocated you have, and if there are any questions, in particular, that you -- the Trial Chamber -- the Appeals Chamber would be interested in having you address. Yes, Mr. Praljak, your counsel are not here, of course. Would you like to raise any issue yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not want to raise any issue, but I wish to correct you on one point. You've said - maybe you've misspoke - that the submission says that the Tribunal owes me some dues. It is quite the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That may have been a mistake in interpretation. I certainly didn't say that. I said exactly the opposite. Okay, thank you for pointing it out. And I would like someone then to check this with the transcript or the translation of the transcript because, as Mr. Praljak pointed out, it's not the Tribunal that owes him money but it's he that owes a huge amount of money to the Tribunal. Mr. Petkovic or his counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have nothing further. What Mr. Stringer raised is something that is a concern to all of us because we all have other commitments, and it's important for us to prepare for this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PLAVEC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And counsel for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation][Via videolink] Your Honour, at this point, the Defence of Mr. Pusic has nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. I have got nothing else to raise myself either. So since there are no other matters to be raised or discussed, I bring this Status Conference to an end, and I thank you all for your attendance. And I adjourn these proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 9.54 a.m.
